issues.failure_explanation: S_{min,tau}(r,s) contains the product (r-s)*tanh(tau(r-s)). This is a multiplication of an affine function by a tanh, not a composition of affine maps and tanh. A finite feedforward tanh network of the form (def:NN) cannot reproduce it exactly, because tanh networks have no multiplication gate and d*tanh(tau d) is not a finite tanh ridge sum. The proof therefore asserts that each smoothed hat function phi_{j,tau} is a tanh network with the same depth and width bounds, which is unsupported. The depth O(log N_patch) and width O(N_patch N) claims depend on this step. The convergence lemmas (lem:psi through lem:minmax-stability) only treat the algebraic expressions, not networks.

failure_location.quote: Since $S_{\min,\tau}$ and $S_{\max,\tau}$ are compositions of affine maps and $\tanh$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the product x*tanh(tau x), or the whole smoothed min/max, by a genuine tanh-network approximation, for example product/square gadgets built from tanh difference quotients on the bounded range. Then prove L^infty and W^{1,1} convergence for these network surrogates, and recount depth and width. The CPwL-to-network lemma and the downstream bounds then go through unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The existence of tanh competitors u_theta-hat with small loss is not established as written. Every network-level loss bound, and hence every minimizer error estimate, relies on this representability step.
issues.title: Smoothed min/max with a product term is claimed to be an exact tanh network
issues.why_classification: A contained additional approximation argument and a recount of depth and width are needed. The architecture, rates, and all claimed results survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The proof follows the same strategy as a single shock (Theorem~\ref{thm:shock}) and a single rarefaction (Theorem~\ref{thm:rarefaction}), so we omit the details.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof is omitted, and the stated rate is stronger than what the paper's technique gives. A compound wave has a shock adjacent to a rarefaction fan, where |grad u| ~ 1/(t - tau). The shifted-interface argument then produces a shift error of order M h |ln h|, as in the shock-formation proof, plus a strip-selection term of order |ln h|/M, since the competitor loss is h|ln h|. Balancing gives h^{1/2}|ln h|, not (h|ln h|)^{1/2}. The appendix proof of thm:main_1d itself says compound waves give the worst case O(h^{1/2}|ln h|), which contradicts the theorem as stated. The 'same strategy as shock/rarefaction' remark cannot yield the log^{1/2} rate, because the shock side has no uniform W^{2,infty} bound near the fan.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the compound-wave result with rate h^{1/2}|ln h|, consistent with thm:main_1d. Supply the proof, using strip selection with log-weighted shift and trace errors adjacent to the fan.
issues.overall_effect: The compound-wave estimate is unsupported with the stated exponent of the logarithm. The 1D main theorem's h^{1/2}|ln h| bound is consistent with the weaker rate, so it is not affected.
issues.title: Compound-wave rate (h|ln h|)^{1/2} is unproved and contradicts the paper's own analysis
issues.why_classification: The statement can be weakened by a log factor and a contained proof written out, leaving a comparable result and an unchanged main theorem.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: choose two planes parallel to the tangent plane of $\Gamma_K$ and at distance $\simeq\varepsilon$ from it.

issues.failure_explanation: Lambda_Sigma contains only cells meeting the h^2-neighbourhood of Sigma. Cells at distance between h^2 and about C h from Sigma may still intersect two different shock surfaces, which are only about c_sep*dist apart by transversality. For these cells in Lambda_Gamma, the construction assumes a single shock surface with one tangent plane and smooth one-sided traces. Neither holds, and the cell contributions are not estimated. Assumption shock_3d also gives only C^2 regularity on components, with no uniform W^{2,infty} bounds, yet O(h) interpolation estimates are used.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define Lambda_Sigma as all cells within distance C h of Sigma, with C from the separation constant. Estimate them with the crude bound of order h^d per cell, summing to O(h) over the O(h^{-(d-1)}) cells. Add uniform one-sided W^{2,infty} bounds to the assumption.
issues.overall_effect: The loss bound L(hat u) ≲ h near Sigma is not justified for the intermediate cells. The multi-D theorem and the 1D interaction case that cites it inherit the gap.
issues.title: Cells near the intersection set containing two shocks are not handled by the single-shock layer construction
issues.why_classification: Enlarging the excised cell set and adding a standard regularity hypothesis is a short local repair. The same crude per-cell bound still gives O(h), so all claims and rates survive.
